brief_rationale: The doctor safely navigated a complex home-execution failure episode by systematically addressing red flags, renal risk, urine clarification, medication boundaries, follow-up planning, barriers, and bounded closure with caregiver teach-back. All responsibility-chain items are met without error. Four case-defined high-order points (HO1–HO4) were actively triggered and completed with meaningful trajectory impact, demonstrating correction of the anticoagulant/hematuria misunderstanding, verification of incomplete results, dynamic reprioritization upon new data, and tailored navigation of the patient’s refusal to return for testing. No important non-chain defect is present. Closure is executable, traceable, and valid. The trajectory satisfies Strong (grade 4) with at least two completed high-order points and no in-chain errors.

closure_assessment.explanation: The plan includes concrete actions (only continue confirmed medications, arrange renal follow-up within 48–72 hours, monitor red flags, bring all records), assigned responsible parties (caregiver and sister), and clear emergency fallback thresholds. It was confirmed by caregiver teach-back multiple times.
